cards.text: After the boils (Exodus 9:8-12), Pharaoh, king of Egypt, STILL won't listen, so the LORD sends Moses, Israel's leader, back to stand before him early in the morning. The message hasn't changed: "Let My people go, so that they may worship Me." Friend, that man's alarm clock has to be TIRED of him.

cards.question: If Pharaoh says no, the LORD will send all His plagues against Pharaoh, his officials and his people. What does the LORD want Pharaoh to know?

answers.text: There is no one like the LORD in all the earth
Israel is stronger than the army of Egypt
Moses is the greatest prophet in the land

cards.text: Then the LORD tells Pharaoh that by this time He could have stretched out His hand and struck him and his people with a plague to wipe them off the earth. He could have, but He didn't, and friend, I had to sit down on my gold base for that one.

cards.question: So why hasn't He? The LORD says He raised Pharaoh up to display His power to him, so that His ___ might be proclaimed in all the earth.
The LORD tells Pharaoh that he has finally started letting Israel go.

cards.text: Then comes the warning: "Behold, at this time tomorrow I will rain down the worst hail that has ever fallen on Egypt, from the day it was founded until now." That's not a "grab a jacket" forecast, friend, that's the WORST in Egypt's WHOLE history.

cards.question: The LORD even gives Egypt a heads-up before the hail. What does He tell Pharaoh to give orders to do right now?

answers.text: Shelter the livestock and everything in the field
Send the livestock away to the land of Goshen
Gather the people and pray to the gods of Egypt

cards.question: The LORD warns that every man or beast left out in the field will die when the hail comes down.

cards.text: So the warning's out, and Pharaoh's officials have a choice to make. It's the weather app saying 100% chance of hail, and some folks grab the umbrella while others say, "Eh, they ALWAYS say that."

cards.question: What do the officials who feared the word of the LORD do?

answers.text: Hurry their servants and livestock to shelter
Ask Moses to call off the hail
Move their families into Pharaoh's palace

cards.question: The officials who disregarded the word of the LORD left their servants and livestock in the ___.

cards.text: Then the LORD tells Moses to stretch out his hand toward heaven, so hail falls on all the land of Egypt: on man and beast and every plant of the field. No more forecasts, friend, it's GO time.

cards.question: Moses stretches out his staff toward heaven. Along with the hail, what else does the LORD send?

cards.text: The hail falls with the lightning flashing right through it, and nothing like it had ever been seen in all of Egypt since it became a nation. Friend, this is the storm where every phone in the house blasts an emergency alert at once, and you're under the covers before it's done buzzing.

cards.question: The hail beat down the plants in Egypt's fields, but it left the trees alone.
The hail pounds the land of Egypt. But just like with the flies (Exodus 8:22), there's one place where it doesn't hail at all. Where?

cards.text: Then Pharaoh summons Moses and Aaron, Moses's brother. "This time I have sinned," he says, and friend, I love that "this time," like all those other times we just don't talk about.

cards.question: Pharaoh keeps going. What does he say about the LORD?
Pharaoh has had enough of God's thunder and hail. What does he ask Moses to do?

cards.text: Pharaoh even promises to let them go, and Moses says that once he's left the city, he'll spread out his hands to the LORD and the thunder and hail will stop. Friend, Pharaoh wants this storm GONE, and honestly, I'm right there with him.

cards.question: Moses says the storm will stop so that Pharaoh may know that the earth is the ___.
Moses tells Pharaoh he knows that Pharaoh and his officials finally fear the LORD.

cards.text: Now a quick note in the text: the flax and barley were destroyed, since the barley was ripe and the flax was in bloom. Of all the weeks to be ready, friend, the barley picked THAT one.

cards.question: The wheat and spelt were destroyed by the hail too.

cards.text: Moses leaves Pharaoh, goes out of the city and spreads out his hands to the LORD, and the thunder and hail stop and the rain no longer pours down on the land. Just like that, friend, the sky goes from WORST EVER to not a peep.

cards.question: The sky goes quiet, and Pharaoh sees the storm is over. What does he do?

answers.text: He sins again and hardens his heart
He lets the Israelites go at once
He sends Moses a gift of thanks

cards.question: Pharaoh hardened his heart, and so did his ___.

cards.text: So Pharaoh's heart was hardened, and he wouldn't let the Israelites go, just as the LORD had said through Moses. Keep your apron on, friend, because this story is a long way from done.

findings.problem: "Pharaoh STILL won't listen, so the LORD sends Moses" gives a reason for the LORD sending Moses. Exodus 9:13 gives no reason. It only says the LORD told Moses to get up early and stand before Pharaoh.

rule.text: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: In "that man's alarm clock has to be TIRED of him," the last person named is Pharaoh ("stand before him"), so it isn't clear whose alarm clock is meant. The joke also depends on Moses having gotten up early many times before, and this lesson never sets that up.

rule.text: It clicks instantly for any adult, with no explaining.

findings.problem: Card 1 already says Pharaoh "STILL won't listen." That gives away the answer to the true or false statement that Pharaoh has finally started letting Israel go (Exodus 9:17).

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The weather-app joke says some people grab the umbrella and others ignore the warning. That tells the baker that some officials take shelter (card 10) and some leave everything out (card 11) before either card is asked.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: No card tells that the hail struck down everything in the field, both man and beast (Exodus 9:25). That is what the warning in 9:19 said would happen, and the true or false card only asks about plants and trees. The baker misses an important detail of the passage.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: No card tells that Goshen is where the Israelites lived (Exodus 9:26). Without that, the baker doesn't see that the place the hail spared was Israel's land.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.
